Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Reasoning: Merging the two tests into one dropped the `posted_on` assertion, so `posted_on` behavior is no longer covered, even though Task 4 requires that it "stays covered."
Confidence: high (the diff is small and fully read; no commands were supplied or run)

Findings:
  - [Critical] F1: ledger/importer_test.py:13 — The merge of `test_import_sets_amount` and `test_import_sets_posted_on` into `test_import_maps_fields` lost coverage.
        The merged test asserts `account` and `amount` but not `posted_on`, so a regression in `date.fromisoformat(record["posted_on"])` would now pass.
        The plan requires that existing posted_on behavior "stays covered".
        Fix: Add `assert entry.posted_on == date(2026, 1, 15)` to `test_import_maps_fields`.
        touched-files: ledger/importer_test.py
        touched-resources: none
  - [Minor] F2: [shrink] ledger/importer_test.py:18 — `test_import_trims_memo` loads a 400-record, roughly 60 KB fixture just to read `records[7]`.
        It reaches the file through a relative path, so the test fails when pytest runs from any directory other than the one holding `fixtures/`.
        It also breaks silently if the shared fixture is reordered.
        The behavior under test only reads `memo`.
        Fix: Use `entry = import_record({**RECORD, "memo": "  quarterly fee "}, TODAY)`, then `assert entry.memo == "quarterly fee"`. Drop the `open`/`json.load` lines and the `import json` line.
        touched-files: ledger/importer_test.py
        touched-resources: fixtures/ledger_400.json (no longer read; no edit)
  - [Minor] F3: ledger/importer.py:24 — `record.get("memo", "").strip()` raises `AttributeError` when a record has `"memo": null`.
        Before this change, such a record imported with `memo=None`.
        If null memos can occur in source data, this change turns them into import crashes.
        Fix: If null memos are possible, use `(record.get("memo") or "").strip()`.
        touched-files: ledger/importer.py
        touched-resources: none
